newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia seeks foreign investors for toll roads.
newsitem.headline: Colombia seeks foreign investors for toll roads.

text.p: Colombia's National Highway Institute is looking to attract foreign investors for the construction of toll roads, the institute's director said on Monday.

Guillermo Gaviria said Colombia was looking to offer at least 10 highway construction projects to companies from the United States, France, Spain and Germany. Once built, the companies would hold a 20-year lease on the routes with the right to levy tolls on highway users.
One of the main routes up for grabs is between Tobiagrande and Puerto Salgar in central Cundinamarca province.
The 44-mile (71 km) stretch across mountainous terrain will provide a rapid link between Bogota and the Magdalena Medio highway, which links the center of the country with the Caribbean coast.
The overall cost of the project is expected to exceed $410 million, Gaviria said. The bidding process for the work has already opened and is expected to last about eight months.
Construction work is scheduled to start next year and is expected to be completed by 2002.
